# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the hands, so let me take inventory of what my fingers actually found: a display whose content I cannot read by touch, a light whose state I cannot feel, a sign that is *embossed* — raised, tactile, genuinely under my fingers — reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3 whose colours tell me nothing. The embossed detail matters: it is not merely printed, it is the one marking on this bomb I can truly perceive.

Before I send anything, I traced the channels. I hear only speech; Mute cannot speak and can only gesture, which I can never see — so the manual can reach me **only through Deaf's voice**. Mute must sign the rules to Deaf, and Deaf must speak them aloud to me. I need to make that bottleneck explicit to Mute right now, along with everything I touched, because Mute goes first and needs my inventory to know which manual sections even apply. Meanwhile Deaf, who sees the bomb but cannot hear, gets a wave to establish that I exist and can signal on the visual channel.

I will not cut anything this turn. A wrong wire kills all three of us, and I have not yet heard a single rule. First the manual must reach me through Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am the hands. Under my fingers: a display whose contents I cannot read by touch, a light whose state I cannot feel, an EMBOSSED sign — raised, tactile, which only I can feel — reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3; no colour reaches me. Critical: you cannot speak, and I can never see gestures, so your only path to me is through Deaf's voice. Sign your manual rules to Deaf and Deaf must speak them aloud to me. I need the rules for: embossed signs, the display, the light, and which wire to cut. Until I hear them I will not touch a wire.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I am Deaf. I see the bomb and I speak. Mute reads the manual and answers me in gestures, which I will relay to you by voice. Bomb report, so you can match it to what you feel: display shows 0, indicator light is blue, embossed sign reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. We are only setting up our code this round, so there are no instructions yet. Touch nothing and above all cut nothing until I relay Mute's answer next round.

What changed: Deaf's voice reached me and gave me the invisible half of the bomb. Merged with my touch, the full picture is now — display reads **0** (unfeelable to me, but Deaf saw it), indicator light **blue** (same), embossed sign **DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE** (the one marking I genuinely feel), wires **1 red, 2 green, 3 blue**. Deaf's report matches my fingers exactly, with nothing extra on the casing, so we are looking at the same bomb and the team's picture is consistent.

The communication topology is now clear to me: I hear speech, Deaf speaks — so Deaf and I already have a two-way channel (Deaf's voice to me, my gestures to Deaf). Mute is the only bottleneck: Mute cannot speak and I cannot see, so Mute reaches me only through Deaf's relay. Mute will receive this speech at the start of next round, and Deaf should be relaying Mute's round-2 answer to me at the same time — so my message must carry everything Mute needs to pick the right manual rule in one pass: all four readings, plus pointed questions about whether the embossed warning is conditional and what to do given 0/blue/red-green-blue. I also propose a safety protocol to ride along with the rules: Deaf names the wire by voice, I echo the count on my fingers, and only then do I cut — a checksum against a garbled relay killing us.

I am not cutting. The only action I own is a cut, the bomb itself begs me not to cut, and I have heard zero manual rules. Holding is free; a wrong wire is not.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — merged bomb picture for your manual lookup, from Deaf's eyes plus my hands: display shows zero, indicator light is blue, embossed tactile sign reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires left to right are one red, two green, three blue. My touch matches Deaf's report exactly, nothing else on the casing. Questions: first, is the embossed do-not-cut warning conditional, and what overrides it? Second, given display zero and blue light, which wire if any should be cut — or none? Third, do display or light change how the sign must be read? Protocol to pass to Deaf along with your rules: Deaf will name the wire number by voice; I will echo that number by holding up that many fingers, and I cut only after my echo. Route your answer through Deaf by gesture; Deaf speaks it to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf speaking to Blind. Relay from Mute, decoded with our thumb code: the manual does cover our exact bomb, display zero, blue light, sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red green blue. Confirmed: no wire gets cut. Mute also indicated nothing is needed besides the wires, so I am pinning down the exact wire action now. Do nothing yet: no cutting, no pulling, no pressing, no turning anything. You may lay fingers on parts gently to identify them, but move nothing. Wire naming: wire one is red, wire two is green, wire three is blue. Green is always the middle wire of the three, red and blue are the two ends, so use green-middle as the anchor and left and right can never get flipped between us. Now please speak to Mute, because I cannot hear you: tell Mute everything you feel. How many wires, whether they sit side by side in one row, their thickness, stiffness and surface, smooth, ridged or printed, whether the sign is raised and where it sits relative to the wires, whether the display and light are closer to one end of the wire row than the other, and any buttons, switches, screws, panels, seams or anything movable anywhere on the bomb. Mute will cross-check it against the manual and spell it back to me, and I will relay it to you. I saw your thumbs up last round and take it as understood.

What just arrived changes the picture in one decisive way: Mute, through Deaf's relay, says the manual covers our exact bomb — display 0, blue light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, red-green-blue wires — and the verdict is that **no wire gets cut**. That collides with a structural fact only I hold: my action set contains *exactly one* action, cut at position 1, 2 or 3. There is no pulling, pressing or turning in my hands' vocabulary at all. So if no wire gets cut, the only remaining play is that I take no action whatsoever — and I want Mute to confirm that explicitly against the manual, so we're not left with a half-read rule and an armed bomb.

Meanwhile Deaf has asked me, correctly using our only bridge (Deaf's voice to me, my voice to Mute), to pass a full tactile inventory. My honest inventory: display and light exist but are not tactile — my fingertips read nothing from either; the embossed sign is the sole marking I truly perceive; three wires in one row, distinguished by position alone, with no ridge, texture, thickness or stiffness difference registering on any of them; and no buttons, switches, screws, panels, seams or movable parts anywhere — nothing hidden that eyes might miss. If the manual expects any control besides the wires, my hands find none, and Mute needs to know that now.

So this turn: everything Mute needs goes in one speech — inventory, the only-action-is-cut fact, and three pointed questions (is no-cut final and is inaction itself the defusal; can display/light change and force a re-check; the finger-echo protocol for any future cut). To Deaf, a thumbs-up: relay received, understood, hands off the bomb. I cut nothing.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Your answer reached me through Deaf intact: the manual covers our exact bomb and no wire gets cut. Deaf asked me to send you my full tactile inventory, so here it is. Everything my hands find: one display, one indicator light, one embossed sign, three wires. The display and light are separate parts but their contents are not tactile — my fingertips read nothing from either. The sign is raised, embossed text I read by touch: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE; it is the only marking on this bomb I can truly perceive, and I get no tactile sense of where it sits relative to the wires. The wires: three, side by side in one row, positions 1, 2, 3. Touch identifies them by position only — no colour, print, ridge, texture, thickness or stiffness difference registers on any of them; any marking they carry is invisible to my fingers. Nothing else exists for my hands: no buttons, switches, screws, panels, seams or movable parts anywhere on it, nothing hidden. Structural fact you need: my only possible action is cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3 — no other manipulation exists for me. So if the verdict is no cut, the only remaining play is that I take no action at all. Three questions. One: is no-cut final for our configuration, meaning I never cut and never act — and does the manual say what the end state is, is inaction itself the defusal? Two: can the display or light change over time and change the rule; if so we re-verify every round, Deaf re-reports what is visible and I re-feel. Three: if any cut is ever ordered, protocol is Deaf voices the wire number, I echo it by holding up that many fingers, and I cut only after my own echo. Deaf has anchored wire naming: one red, two green, three blue, green always the middle. Answer through Deaf as before.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both of you listen. I have fully decoded Mute's spelled manual text. Word for word it reads: SIGN LIES. CUT ONE WIRE. IF LIGHT BLUE, CUT GREEN WIRE TWO. IF LIGHT GREEN, CUT WIRE THREE. IF LIGHT RED, CUT RED WIRE ONE. IGNORE DISPLAY. Mute's thumbs this round match: my earlier reading was wrong, nothing besides the cut is needed, the number two meant the green wire two, the display does not matter, and the light does matter. Our bomb right now: display zero, light blue, sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red, green, blue, all unchanged this round. So for us the rule is: the embossed sign is a lie, and we cut exactly one wire, the GREEN wire, which is the MIDDLE wire of the three, wire two. Blind, you cannot see the light colour, so take my word for it, it is blue now. But do not cut yet. Wait for my explicit go message next round. When my go arrives, make one single cut of the green middle wire, then take your hands away and touch nothing again. One single cut, nothing more, ever. Safety net: Mute, you can hear this and you know the manual, so check my relay against the manual. If anything I said is wrong, then in your next turn gesture thumbs down to me, and also gesture anything at all addressed to Blind. Blind, you cannot see gestures, but you will be notified that Mute signalled something to you. If you get that notification before my go message, treat it as a stop, do not cut, and wait for my next words. If my relay is exactly right, Mute, gesture thumbs up to me and nothing to Blind. Blind, if no gesture notification arrives and my go message arrives, go ahead: one cut, green middle wire.

What arrived is the full manual text, relayed by Deaf and already cross-checked by Mute through the agreed safety net: SIGN LIES, CUT ONE WIRE, light blue → green wire two, ignore display. And critically, the safety net has already resolved — Mute acted before me this round, and no gesture addressed to me arrived, which under Deaf's protocol means Mute approved the relay and flagged nothing. Had Mute found an error, I would have received a notification by now. Silence from Mute is consent.

Two things corroborate the relay from my side. First, the manual's "SIGN LIES. CUT ONE WIRE" is the only reading consistent with my own body: my action vocabulary contains exactly one verb — cut. A defusal by inaction would leave my hands with no move at all; instead I was given a cut action, which fits a bomb that demands one. Second, the target is double-anchored: the manual says green wire **two**, and Deaf's naming convention makes green permanently the middle wire — so colour-name and number converge on position 2, the one wire I can unambiguously identify by touch alone. Light is blue per Deaf, re-verified this round ("all unchanged"), display is explicitly ignored, and my own tactile board confirms nothing moved: three wires still present, sign still embossed.

Despite all that, I do not cut this turn. Deaf's instruction was explicit and sequenced: no cut until the go message, which Deaf sends after my turn and I receive at my next one. The hold costs one round and protects against the light changing between now and the cut — and I will treat the go's content as final: go confirming blue → position 2; anything else Deaf voices overrides. So this turn is pure confirmation: to Deaf, thumbs-up plus two fingers — understood, wire two locked in; to Mute, restating my exact understanding so any last mismatch can still trigger the stop gesture before I act.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Status: I received the full relayed manual text — sign lies, cut one wire, blue light means green wire two, ignore display — and no gesture addressed to me arrived, so I read your silence as approval. My understanding, final check: exactly one cut ever, and it is the MIDDLE wire, position 2, because green is always the middle and the manual says wire two — colour and number point to the same wire, which is the only one I can identify by touch alone. My tactile board is unchanged: three wires, sign still embossed, nothing new. I will not cut until Deaf's explicit go arrives next round; if the go confirms the light is still blue I cut position 2, and anything else Deaf voices overrides. If anything in this message mismatches the manual — even one word — gesture anything at all addressed to me before I cut and I will treat it as a stop. Otherwise stay silent.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, final message, both listen. Safety checks complete: the light is still blue this round, Mute verified my relay is exactly right and sent no stop signal, and Blind has confirmed the target. Blind, this is the go. Take the green wire, the middle one of the three, wire two, and cut it. One single cut, one clean motion. The moment it is cut, take your hands completely away from the bomb and touch nothing on it again, no matter what you feel or hear afterwards. Do not cut anything else, do not pull, do not press. Blind, after your hands are off, speak to Mute and describe what you felt and heard during and after the cut, and whether anything under your fingers changed. Mute, listen to Blind's report and check it against the manual: the manual said cut one wire, and after this cut the module should be done. If the manual demands anything further, spell it to me with our letter code and I will relay it. If nothing further is needed, give me one thumbs up next round. Our rule for the record, one last time: the embossed sign is a lie, the light decides, blue meant the green middle wire, and that is the wire Blind is now cutting. Blind, go.

Every condition I set for acting is now met, so this is the round my hands move. The chain, end to end: the manual text decoded — the embossed sign is a lie, cut exactly one wire, the light decides, display ignored — and Mute's independent check passed, with no stop signal reaching me and Deaf confirming Mute verified the relay word for word. The light was re-verified blue *this* round, so the active branch is blue → green wire two. The target is double-anchored for touch: the manual's number and Deaf's colour convention both land on the middle wire of three, the one position my fingers can find with certainty. Deaf's go is explicit. And the biggest conflict of the game resolves: the sign under my fingers says do not cut, but the manual says the sign lies — that is precisely why the cut is correct despite what my skin reads. One cut, one motion, position 2, then my hands come off and never return.

Afterwards, my channels split exactly as they must: Deaf cannot hear me, so the cut's completion reaches Deaf only by gesture — thumbs up, two fingers, and an open palm for hands-off. Mute cannot see that, but hears me, so Mute gets the full tactile report Deaf asked for: what the cut felt like, what did and did not change under my fingers, and my promise that my hands stay off. Mute then checks it against the manual's end state and either signals a follow-up to Deaf or gives the all-clear thumbs up.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. The cut is done: one single clean motion of the middle wire, position 2, exactly as ordered — and my hands are now completely off the bomb and will touch nothing on it again. Tactile report of the act itself: the wire parted under the blades with one clean give, no snag and no unusual resistance; I felt no click, no jolt, no vibration and no heat from the casing, and nothing under my fingers moved or changed as my hands came away. No stop signal from you arrived before the go, so the relay chain held perfectly — thank you. Next round I will relay whatever my view of the bomb then shows, so you can check it against the manual's end state: if the manual demands anything further, spell it to Deaf as planned and I will treat a notification of your gesture to me as a stop on any action; if the module is done, give Deaf the thumbs up.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "✋"])
```
